about: How many trials each ticket gets in an adaptive campaign (QA eval with trials: adaptive; eval/trials.ts). The allocation is fixed from the history before the campaign starts, and never changed by its results: no ticket stops early because its first trials look good. A ticket left uncertain by the release decision gets follow-up trials, and the decision is taken again on all its trials together. node eval/trials.ts backtest measures, on the history, what this saves and what it misses.

why.stable_trials: A ticket stable in the history (stable, below) gets 2 trials: if either fails, its outcome changed, and the release decision asks for a rerun before anything else.
why.default_trials: Every other ticket gets the 3 trials of a uniform campaign.
why.risky_trials: A ticket never run with its current corpus, regressed in the last regression_lookback changes of version, or unstable in the latest version that ran it, gets 5 trials: it is where a change is likeliest, and where 3 trials tell it least well from variation.
why.critical_trials: A critical ticket (eval/compare-policy.json) gets 5 trials, whatever its history: a confirmed regression there rejects a version. The two critical tickets are also the cheapest to run.
why.follow_up_trials: When the release decision asks for a rerun of a ticket, it gets 3 more trials, and the decision pools them with the first ones.
why.stable: Stable: every trial passed in each of the last 2 versions that ran the ticket with its current corpus, over 6 trials or more.
